q-156691.name: Question 1
q-156691.problem: Which of the following diagrams shows the graph of $y={log}_{10}⁡x?$
q-156691.worked_solution:
Let's recall some of the basic properties of $y={log}_{10}⁡x:$

- The domain is $x>0$, and the range is $-\infty <y<\infty .$

- The graph has the vertical asymptote $x=0.$

- The function is an increasing function.

- The graph passes through the point $(1,0).$

- For $x>1$, the graph is positive and grows very slowly as we increase $x.$ We say that $y\to \infty $ (slowly) as $x\to \infty .$

Of the given functions, the only one that has all of these properties is as follows:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14245974/assets/5a52b4fcfb2cc410c894f69771ff450ceef1366048438345d1444e35186d9d76.png)

q-47626.name: Question 8
q-47626.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y=\operatorname{log}⁡x?$

I. The function passes through the point $(1,0)$

II. Its horizontal asymptote is $y=0.$

III. It passes through the point $(10,100).$
q-47626.worked_solution:
Let's plot the graph of $y=\operatorname{log}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14245974/assets/177d2949118515d96b6a1c49d0222a2417ab6236e8641f8d89c0cd8f6b30a592.png)

Let's go through each statement.

- Statement I is true.

- Statement II is false. The function $y=\operatorname{log}⁡x$ has no horizontal asymptote. However, it does have the vertical asymptote $x=0.$

- Statement III is false. Substituting $x=10$ into the equation of the curve gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\operatorname{log}⁡(10) \\  & =\operatorname{log}⁡({10}^{1}) \\  & =1\ne 100\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, only statement I is true.

Let's plot the graph of y=log⁡x.

In conclusion, only statement I is true.

q-156743.name: Question 9
q-156743.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y={log}_{6}⁡x?$ 

I. It has no zeros

II. $y\to 6$ as $x\to \infty $

III. It has a vertical asymptote at $x=0$
q-156743.worked_solution:
Let's plot the graph of $y={log}_{6}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14245974/assets/d8d3f9dc995d8801d451b15129860362efa772178cdc3ef07be5adb6a1da5c45.png)

Let's go through each statement.

- Statement I is false. The function has a zero at $x=1.$

- Statement II is false. As $x$ increases, $y$ increases without bound. Therefore, $y\to \infty $ as $x\to \infty $

- Statement III is true.

In conclusion, only statement III is true.

q-156742.name: Question 10
q-156742.problem:
Which of the following statements are true regarding the function $y={log}_{8}⁡x?$

I. The domain is $x\ge 0$

II. It has no horizontal asymptotes

III. It passes through the point $(64,2)$
q-156742.worked_solution:
Let's plot the graph of $y={log}_{8}⁡x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14245974/assets/6811e57f1259b97448811ac9abe8d6fc7f76a52b62e685f2fa0ec36e290381b4.png)

Let's go through each statement.

- Statement I is false. From the graph, we see that the domain is $x>0.$

- Statement II is true. Indeed, the function $y={log}_{8}⁡x$ has no horizontal asymptote. However, it does have the vertical asymptote $x=0.$

- Statement III is true. Substituting $x=64$ into the equation of the curve gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={log}_{8}⁡(64) \\  & ={log}_{8}⁡({8}^{2}) \\  & =2{log}_{8}⁡(8) \\  & =2\,\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, only statements II and III are true.
